sections.heading: Executive Summary & Strategic Scope
sections.source_citation: GoTo 2025 Annual Report, pp. 8, 76-84, 147-152
paragraphs: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (IDX: GOTO) operates across Indonesia's digital economy through On-Demand Services (Gojek mobility, GoFood delivery, logistics), Financial Technology (GoPay payments, consumer lending, merchant solutions), and e-commerce service fees post-Tokopedia deconsolidation.

Prepared by Group 4 (Fagly Ramschie, Anggreini Ruitan, Galatia Rompas) for the Magister Manajemen Universitas Klabat Financial Statement Analysis course, this milestone links Porter's Five Forces industry structure to GoTo's FY2025 cost structure and risk profile for a Public Equity Investor.

sections.heading: 1.1 Company Overview & 2025 Ecosystem Scale
sections.source_citation: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 8, 14-18, 41, 63, 150-158; Consolidated Income Statement p. 17
paragraphs: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk is an Indonesian technology ecosystem formed from Gojek and Tokopedia. It connects consumers, driver-partners, merchants, sellers, and financial-service users on a single shared infrastructure while retaining a 24.99% associate stake in Tokopedia.

In FY2025, GoTo generated Rp 18.322 trillion in consolidated net revenue (+15.3% YoY) and improved Adjusted Group EBITDA to Rp 2.008 trillion, yet still posted a statutory consolidated operating loss of Rp 378.254 billion due to heavy sales, marketing, and technology investments.

sections.heading: 1.2 Industry Overview & Digital Market Structure
sections.source_citation: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 40, 46, 147, 168-169; Meilina (2025); Ahdiat (2026); Ridwan (2026)
paragraphs: GoTo competes in Indonesia's on-demand mobility/delivery, e-commerce services, and digital financial services markets. Network effects let multi-product platforms spread technology overhead across higher transaction frequency.

Macro demand continues expanding: Indonesia's 2025 digital economy reached ~USD 99 billion in GMV, digital payments reached ~USD 538 billion in GTV, digital lending reached ~USD 13 billion, and online transport and food delivery reached ~USD 10 billion GMV. However, multi-homing across Grab, Maxim, inDrive, ShopeeFood, DANA, OVO, and ShopeePay keeps customer acquisition intensity high.

sections.heading: 2.1 Threat of New Entrants (Low to Moderate)
sections.source_citation: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 8, 63, 76-84, 180-183
paragraphs: GoTo's Threat of New Entrants is rated Low to Moderate. Matching GoTo's nationwide two-sided network (66 million ATUs, 6.4 million+ merchants, 3 million+ driver-partners) requires massive capital, cybersecurity architecture, and Bank Indonesia / OJK payment and lending licenses.

However, single-segment app entrants (low-commission ride-hailing or niche wallets) can still chip away at specific local corridors without replicating the entire ecosystem, preventing the rating from being purely Low.

sections.heading: 2.2 Bargaining Power of Suppliers (Low)
sections.source_citation: GoTo Annual Report 2025, p. 325; Consolidated Financial Statements Note 26
paragraphs: GoTo's Bargaining Power of Suppliers is rated Low. Formal procurement governance, competitive bidding under its Vendor Code of Conduct, and an asset-light digital service structure eliminate dependence on physical raw-material suppliers.

In FY2025, no third-party supplier exceeded 10% of consolidated net revenue (Note 26), keeping procurement pricing controllable despite modest foreign-currency exposure on specialized global cloud infrastructure.

sections.heading: 2.3 Bargaining Power of Buyers (Medium)
sections.source_citation: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 8, 56, 148, 152, 168-169; Note 25
paragraphs: GoTo's Bargaining Power of Buyers is rated Medium. Everyday consumers are price-sensitive and compare promos across apps easily, requiring ongoing cashback, shipping subsidies, and tiered pricing between mass-market affordability and affluent speed/quality tiers.

Buyer power does not escalate to High because the customer base is vastly fragmented: 66 million ATUs and 6.4 million merchants ensure that no single customer represents 10% or more of consolidated net revenue (Note 25).

sections.heading: 2.4 Threat of Substitute Products or Services (Medium)
sections.source_citation: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 77-82, 147
paragraphs: GoTo's Threat of Substitutes is rated Medium. Users can fulfill identical daily needs offline or outside super-app ecosystems: public transit instead of GoRide, dine-in cooking/eating instead of GoFood, and debit cards, cash, or direct bank BI-FAST transfers instead of GoPay.

GoTo actively co-opts these substitutes by embedding them inside its platform: GoTransit bundles KAI Commuter rail tickets with first-mile/last-mile GoRide, GoDineIn monetizes restaurant visits, and GoPay links directly to bank accounts.

sections.heading: 2.5 Competitive Rivalry Among Existing Firms (High - Strongest Force)
paragraphs: Competitive Rivalry is rated High and represents the single strongest structural constraint on GoTo's margins. Every core GoTo vertical battles well-funded domestic and regional incumbents with overlapping service menus and zero exclusivity on user devices.

Market data places GrabFood at 46% of 2025 Indonesian online food-delivery GMV versus GoFood at 31% and ShopeeFood at 23%. To defend engagement, GoTo increased 2025 sales & marketing expense 8% to Rp 3.090 trillion and product development 23% to Rp 2.152 trillion, keeping operating EBIT negative (-Rp 378.3 billion).

sections.heading: 3. GoTo's Hybrid Strategic Position
paragraphs: GoTo pursues a hybrid strategic position combining targeted cost leadership (lower cost-to-serve and mass-market affordability via GoFood Saver and streamlined G&A) with ecosystem differentiation (Gojek + GoPay integration, personalization, and brand trust for higher-value urban users).

This dual approach aligns directly with Five Forces: low supplier leverage allows cloud/operating efficiencies, while Medium buyer power and High rivalry force GoTo to deliver both competitive pricing and multi-product convenience to sustain user retention.

sections.heading: 4.1-4.3 Core Strategic, Substitution & Fintech Credit Risks
sections.source_citation: GoTo Annual Report 2025, pp. 14-18, 46, 56-57, 77-82, 152, 180-183; Consolidated Statements Note 35
paragraphs: Three interlocking risks translate Five Forces directly into financial-statement risk: (4.1) Pricing & promo margin compression (defending orders can reignite subsidy spend above gross profit), (4.2) Customer switching & multi-homing across substitutes (reducing transaction frequency and take rates), and (4.3) Fintech credit and regulatory risk.

Note 35 reveals concrete balance-sheet exposure from GoPay lending: net financing and lending receivables surged +72.6% to Rp 2.731 trillion in 2025 (from Rp 1.582T in 2024), while allowance for impairment losses more than doubled (+134.9%) from Rp 173.552 billion to Rp 407.684 billion alongside heightened Bank Indonesia / OJK compliance mandates.

sections.heading: 5. Overall Strategic Assessment & References
sections.source_citation: Milestone 1 Final Group 4 Write-Up & Bibliography
paragraphs: Conclusion: Indonesia's digital platform industry combines robust macro expansion with demanding structural profitability barriers. GoTo holds defensible barriers to entry and low supplier leverage, but High competitive rivalry and Medium buyer/substitute power prevent easy margin expansion.

Overall attractiveness for a new entrant is only moderate, while for incumbent GoTo the decisive investment variable tested in Milestones 2-4 is whether ecosystem monetization and Fintech lending growth can yield durable GAAP net income above cost of equity without escalating credit losses or draining cash.

sections.heading: Executive Ratio & DuPont Package Overview
sections.source_citation: Group 4 Milestone 2 Workbook (Historical Data, Ratios, DuPont, Peer Benchmark)
paragraphs: Milestone 2 evaluates PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk's financial health across FY2023-FY2025 using its Common-Size statements, Liquidity, Efficiency, Solvency, Profitability, 3-Step DuPont ROE, Peer Benchmark vs. Bukalapak, and Emerging-Market Altman Z''-Score.

Core finding: GoTo materially narrowed its operating loss (from -69.5% to -2.1% of revenue) and maintains a strong cash liquidity cushion (Current Ratio 2.73x, Cash = 47.5% of Assets), yet still generates negative ROE (-5.2%), negative ROA (-3.3%), and a Distress-Zone Z''-Score (-10.90) driven by -Rp 214.1 trillion of accumulated deficit.

Revenue grew +7.5% in 2024 and +15.3% in 2025 to Rp 18.322 trillion. Because COGS grew only +4.5% in 2025 while operating expenses edged up +2.2%, operating loss narrowed from Rp 10.279 trillion (2023) to Rp 2.241 trillion (2024) and Rp 378.254 billion (2025), and net loss shrank to Rp 1.502 trillion.

sections.heading: 2. Vertical Common-Size Analysis (Income Statement & Balance Sheet)
sections.source_citation: Group 4 M2 Workbook, Common-Size Analysis Tab; LK GOTO 2025 pp. 15-17
paragraphs: Common-size income statement weights confirm structural cost discipline: COGS dropped from 46.6% of revenue in 2024 to 42.3% in 2025 (lifting gross margin from 53.4% to 57.7%), while total operating expenses fell from 135.1% (2023) to 59.8% (2025). Yet OpEx (59.8%) still exceeds Gross Margin (57.7%), explaining the remaining -2.1% operating loss margin.

On the common-size balance sheet, Cash remains the anchor asset at 47.5% of Total Assets (Rp 21.755T), while Total Liabilities expanded from 29.6% (2024) to 37.3% (2025) and Equity declined from 70.4% to 62.7% due to continuing losses.

sections.heading: 3. Liquidity & Working Capital Efficiency Analysis
sections.source_citation: Group 4 M2 Workbook, Ratio Analysis Tab; LK GOTO 2025 p. 15
paragraphs: GoTo's short-term liquidity remained exceptionally solid in FY2025 with both Current Ratio and Quick Ratio at 2.73x, backed by positive working capital of Rp 18.412 trillion.

Operating efficiency also improved meaningfully: Total Asset Turnover rose from 0.27x (2023) to 0.40x (2025), closing-balance DSO improved to 10.9 days (trade receivables Rp 547.3 bn), and the Cash Conversion Cycle stayed negative at -47.5 days, meaning GoTo collects cash from platform transactions weeks before paying suppliers.

sections.heading: 4. Solvency, Debt Doubling & Profitability Trajectory
sections.source_citation: Group 4 M2 Workbook, Ratio Analysis Tab; Audited LK Note 19 & 20
paragraphs: Although overall leverage remains moderate (mostly equity-funded at 62.7% of assets), total interest-bearing debt more than doubled in FY2025 from Rp 3.820 trillion to Rp 7.743 trillion, pushing Debt-to-Equity from 0.13x to 0.27x and Debt-to-Total-Assets from 8.8% to 16.9%.

Despite gross margin recovering to 57.7% and operating loss narrowing to -2.1%, profitability remains negative: ROA was -3.3% and ROE was -5.2%, leaving Interest Coverage negative (-0.71x on Rp 535 bn interest expense).

sections.heading: 5. Three-Step DuPont ROE Decomposition
sections.source_citation: Group 4 M2 Workbook, DuPont Analysis Tab
paragraphs: The 3-Step DuPont identity (ROE = Net Profit Margin x Asset Turnover x Equity Multiplier) demonstrates that GoTo's ROE recovery from -253.4% (2023) to -18.0% (2024) and -5.2% (2025) was driven overwhelmingly by loss-narrowing margin gains (+604 percentage points) and higher asset productivity (+0.13x turnover).

Financial leverage played only a secondary role (Equity Multiplier rose modestly from 1.51x to 1.59x), meaning GoTo's operational recovery is genuine efficiency rather than debt engineering, though negative net margin still forces ROE below zero.

sections.heading: 6. Peer Comparison (GoTo vs. Bukalapak) & Strategic Conclusion
sections.source_citation: Group 4 M2 Workbook, Peer Benchmark Tab; Bukalapak & GoTo FY2025 Financial Statements
paragraphs: Comparing FY2025 ratios against Indonesian digital peer PT Bukalapak.com Tbk (BUKA) highlights two sharply contrasting financial profiles. GoTo generates 60% higher asset productivity (0.40x Asset Turnover vs. Bukalapak's 0.25x), confirming stronger ecosystem monetization per rupiah of assets.

However, Bukalapak holds zero debt (0.00x Debt-to-Equity), an ultra-high 37.07x current ratio, and positive +48.4% net margin (+12.4% ROE) buoyed by treasury investment income, whereas GoTo remains loss-making. Conclusion: GoTo's primary vulnerability is not short-term liquidity (2.73x), but proving durable profitability without jeopardizing its competitive ecosystem.

Banks need an adapted DuPont model. A bank's 'revenue' (interest and fee income) is itself a return on its main asset (loans), so the standard Net Margin × Asset Turnover pairing becomes definitionally circular. Financial institutions are conventionally analyzed with the 2-factor form: ROE = ROA × Equity Multiplier.

Leverage tells the real story here. BBCA's equity multiplier (5.63x) versus MAPI's (1.60x) reflects a structural difference, not a performance difference ,  banks are inherently far more leveraged than retailers because deposits (a liability) fund the core business. Never compare equity multipliers across sectors without this context.

Even 'real' benchmark data varies by source. The ROE implied by the approximate figures above for MAPI (≈11.1%) differs from the more precise, externally reported figure (≈15.3%) ,  a reminder to always check which total-assets/equity snapshot and date a reported ratio is actually built on before comparing it to your own calculation.

Data currency: figures reflect FY2025 results as reported in company announcements and third-party financial data aggregators available as of early 2026. Verify against each company's primary audited annual report before using precise figures in graded work.

title: Accounting Quality, Cash Flow Forensics & Non-Recurring Items
summary: Forensic audit of Tokopedia & Bank Jago recoverability (22.57% of assets), Accrual Ratios (-11.21% -> -3.95%), analytical earnings adjustments, gross/net revenue policies, and negative Free Cash Flow (-Rp 875.3 bn).

sections.heading: Executive Accounting Quality Summary
sections.source_citation: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (2026). Consolidated Financial Statements 31 Dec 2025
paragraphs: Milestone 3 examines GoTo's 2024-2025 consolidated accounting quality (all tables in Rp million) based strictly on the audited FY2025 financial statements issued in March 2026 (PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk, 2026).

Four red flags and forensic checks define our risk view: (1) 22.57% of total assets reside in Tokopedia and Bank Jago associates alongside Rp 1.669T Level 3 investments; (2) Related-party revenue climbed to 7.13%; (3) Analytical adjustments excluding repeated valuation losses temporarily flip pre-tax profit to +84,062 mn before returning to -165,038 mn after removing associate profits; and (4) Headline +519.1 bn Investing Cash Flow hides -875.3 bn negative Free Cash Flow funded by Rp 1,386.5 bn time-deposit settlements.

sections.heading: (a) Investment Recoverability, 20% Write-Down Test & Revenue Judgment
paragraphs: Tokopedia and Bank Jago carried balances of Rp 7,432,326 million and Rp 2,894,921 million respectively in 2025, together representing 22.57% of GoTo's total assets and embedding Rp 2,003,559 million of goodwill. Separately, GoTo holds Rp 1,668,574 million in Level 3 private investments (Notes 14-15, pp. 100-103).

Under our Week 10 stress test asking what happens if Tokopedia (7,432,326 mn, already inclusive of goodwill) and Level 3 investments (1,668,574 mn) suffer a 20% write-down, every Rp 100 falls to Rp 80. Total assumed impairment is Rp 1,820,180 million, wiping out 3.98% of GoTo's Rp 45,757,642 million asset base before tax. Meanwhile, related-party revenue rose to Rp 1,306,110 million (7.13% of total revenue), warranting ongoing contract and margin scrutiny.

sections.heading: (c) Analytical Adjustments: Removing Valuation Charges & Associate Swings
sections.source_citation: GoTo (2026), Consolidated Income Statement p. 17 & Note 15 p. 103
paragraphs: We keep GoTo's statutory PSAK result as the primary baseline, then analytically adjust Pre-Tax Loss (EBT) for non-operating valuation charges: goodwill impairment (356,830 mn in 2025), PP&E/intangible impairment (217,133 mn), and fair-value losses (596,703 mn, which already include the Level 3 loss). Adding back those Rp 1,170,666 mn charges flips 2025 pre-tax loss (-1,086,604 mn) into a modest +84,062 mn gain.

However, once we also reverse GoTo's non-core share of associate/JV profit in 2025 (-249,100 mn vs. adding back -2,305,125 mn loss in 2024), adjusted pre-tax performance returns to a loss of -(165,038) mn in 2025! Moreover, because impairments occurred in both years and tax effects are unadjusted, excluding them risks overstating sustainable profitability, leaving the statutory -378,254 mn operating loss intact.

sections.heading: (d) Revenue Recognition Policies, Principal vs. Agent & Customer Incentives
sections.source_citation: GoTo (2026), Note 2s (pp. 66-67, 71), Note 25 Related Parties (p. 129)
paragraphs: For GOJEK mobility and food delivery transactions, GoTo acts as an Agent under PSAK 72 / IFRS 15 because it arranges services without controlling underlying driver capacity or restaurant goods, recognizing only its net service fee upon trip/order completion. By contrast, Tokopedia e-commerce consultancy fees are recognized over time based on Tokopedia GMV multiplied by the contracted fee rate (Note 2s, pp. 66-71).

Crucially, customer incentives (promos, cashback, discounts) reduce net revenue directly when GoTo receives no distinct good or service in return; incentives exceeding related expected revenue reclassify into selling and marketing expenses. Connection to Milestone 2: while 15.3% revenue growth and the gross-margin rise (53.4% -> 57.7%) reflect real efficiency, lower customer contra-revenue incentives heavily influence net revenue trajectory without implying policy manipulation.

sections.heading: (e) Investing Cash Flow Check & Negative Free Cash Flow (-Rp 875.3 bn)
sections.source_citation: GoTo (2026), Consolidated Cash Flow Statement p. 21, Balance Sheet p. 15, Note 32 p. 139
paragraphs: Although GoTo generated +307,025 mn in FY2025 Operating Cash Flow, that inflow covered only 25.97% of its 1,182,360 mn total cash CapEx (302,071 mn fixed assets + 880,289 mn intangible assets), leaving a negative Free Cash Flow deficit of -(875,335) mn. Note 32 clarifies that cash CapEx excludes non-cash lease additions totaling the net PP&E balance of 622,356 mn.

Crucially, GoTo's headline +519,117 mn Net Investing Cash Flow was positive solely due to +1,386,520 mn in net time-deposit settlements! Excluding time-deposit Treasury liquidations reveals a true underlying investing cash outflow of -(867,403) mn (even after 216,579 mn explicit investment sales, equal to 18.3% of CapEx).

sections.heading: Task 1B: Degree of Operating Leverage (DOL) & Breakeven Sensitivity
sections.source_citation: LK GOTO 2025 p. 17 & Note 26 Expense by Nature p. 130 (Cost Structure Analysis)
paragraphs: Empirical DOL (% change in operating income / % change in revenue) is only economically meaningful when operating income is positive in both periods. Because GoTo posted operating losses in both 2024 (-2,240.9 bn) and 2025 (-378.3 bn), mechanical DOL (-5.44x empirical; -27.96x cost-structure in 2025) cannot be used directly to project standard positive-profit sensitivity.

Cost-behavior insight & -10% Revenue Shock: Total non-COGS operating expenses rose only +2.17% in 2025 (from Rp 10,721.9 bn to Rp 10,954.3 bn) while revenue jumped +15.27%, proving largely fixed short-run overhead (Operations & Support -0.11%, D&A +0.59%, combined Selling & G&A -2.31%). Yet against Full Operating Expenses (Rp 10,954.3 bn / 57.72% GM = Rp 18,977.4 bn breakeven revenue), GoTo stays 3.58% BELOW breakeven; a hypothetical -10% revenue drop widens statutory EBIT loss from -(378.3) bn to -(1,435.9) bn.

sections.heading: (f) Multi-Method Valuation Reconciliation vs. Rp 25.00 Share Price (Assignment 14)

paragraphs: At WACC = 7.76% and Cost of Equity = 8.45% (Beta = 0.59), intrinsic Base Case models assign negative equity values (DCF = -Rp 121.1/share; Residual Income = -Rp 75.1/share), whereas peer multiples (2.30x P/B & 13.25x Net-Cash EV/EBITDA across BUKA, GRAB, SE, BELI) indicate Rp 39.8/share because relative multiples ignore GoTo's Base Case cash burn.

paragraphs: Target Stakeholder: Public Equity Investor evaluating PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (IDX: GOTO) at Rp 25.00 per share.

One-Sentence Recommendation: SELL GOTO at Rp 25.00 because negative ROE (-5.2%), negative Free Cash Flow (-Rp 875.3 bn), and Base Case cash burn yield negative intrinsic value under both DCF (-Rp 121.1/share) and Residual Income (-Rp 75.1/share). Under our Milestone 4 Base Case, scaling historical 78.5% opex and 16.3% CapEx drives ongoing EBIT losses and drains cash from Rp 21.76T to Rp 968 bn by 2028F. Even though GoTo holds Rp 13.20/share in Net Cash, investors should SELL until management sustains fixed-cost discipline (OpEx <= Rp 10.95T), generates two consecutive years of positive FCF after CapEx, and earns GAAP Net Income above its Rp 2.43T annual equity capital charge (8.45% Ke).
